subject: Hyperion moon
title: Saturn Has a Sponge-Shaped Moon, and It Zapped a Spacecraft

scenes.text: Saturn has a moon that looks like a sponge, and it shot at a spacecraft.
Hyperion is about 170 miles across, and more than 40 percent of it is empty space.
It's so light it would almost float in water, and it tumbles with no regular spin.
In 2014, scientists found that Cassini had flown through a beam of electrons from its surface.
Sunlight and Saturn's magnetic bubble had charged the moon to about minus 200 volts.
It was the first charged surface ever confirmed on a world other than our Moon.

description:
Hyperion, about 270 km across, has a porosity of more than 40% and a density about half that of water, and it tumbles chaotically.
In 2014 scientists reported that during a 2005 flyby Cassini was hit by an electron beam from Hyperion's surface, charged to about minus 200 volts: the first confirmed charged surface on an object other than our Moon.
Which moon in the solar system would you visit first?
first_comment: Hyperion's craters are so deep and sharp because there's so much empty space inside. Would you call it a moon or a rock?
